newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE HOLD LEADERS PSG TO GOALLESS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE HOLD LEADERS PSG TO GOALLESS DRAW.

text.p: Former European champions Marseille showed glimpses of their old form to hold leaders Paris St Germain to a goalless draw at Parc des Princes in the French soccer league on Friday.

Marseille displayed plenty of courage under pressure in the first half and even outplayed the home team after the break as they climbed two places up to ninth in the 20-strong league and extend their unbeaten run to four matches.
The Paris club used the class in midfield of Brazilian stars Rai and Leonardo to dominate the first 45 minutes.
Striker Patrice Loko kept trying but he saw Marseille German Andreas Koepke block all his attempts with several brilliant saves.

Marseille, back to top flight soccer this year after two seasons in the second division following a match-rigging scandal and heavy debts, were stronger in the second half and came close to scoring a couple of times.
Paris stick to the lead but they are now clearly under threat by second-placed Monaco, who will move just one point behind them if they manage to beat lowly Nancy on Saturday.
"It's a good draw by Marseille against a good Paris side and I'm proud of my team," said Marseille trainer Gerard Gili, whose players lifted their arms up in the air after the final whistle.

"Maybe we could have scored but we were not ambitious enough because our main concern was to avoid losing," said Marseille midfielder Eric Roy. "We're playing well at the moment, confidence is back and that's good."
